title: The policy mix
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank covers fiscal, monetary and supply-side policies separately and the conflicts between objectives, but no point teaches coordinating these policies into a mix suited to the problem, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: The policy mix
card: The policy mix is the combination of fiscal, monetary and microeconomic policies a government and the Reserve Bank use together. Fiscal policy is the budget: government spending and taxation. Monetary policy is the setting of interest rates by the Reserve Bank.
Microeconomic policy aims to lift efficiency in particular markets, for example through competition reforms. It mostly works over the longer term and affects the supply side of the economy.
Policies work best when they pull the same way. If fiscal policy boosts demand while monetary policy cuts it, each can weaken the other, so the economy may respond less than intended.
The mix should also suit the problem. Weak demand and rising unemployment call for expansionary settings. Strong demand and rising inflation call for contractionary settings.
draft.remember: Policies work best when they pull the same way and fit the problem the economy faces.

a.q: Why can a government's budget and the Reserve Bank's interest rate settings working against each other be a problem?
opts: Each can weaken the other's effect on demand
Each one makes the other policy unnecessary
Each one raises the other's effect on supply
Each can only be used when the other is paused
a.why: If one policy pushes demand up and the other pushes it down, their effects partly cancel, so the economy responds less than intended. They do not make each other unnecessary, because both are still being used and both still have effects.
a.clue: Think about two pushes in opposite directions.

b.q: Inflation in Australia is rising because demand is very strong. Which mix of fiscal and monetary policy best suits this problem?
opts: Lower government spending and higher interest rates
Lower government spending and lower interest rates
Higher government spending and higher interest rates
Higher government spending and lower interest rates
b.why: Strong demand with rising inflation calls for contractionary settings, and both policies should pull the same way. Lower spending and higher interest rates both slow demand. Higher spending with higher rates pulls in opposite directions, so it is the tempting but weaker choice.
b.clue: Both policies should slow demand, not push it up.

a.best: Each can weaken the other's effect on demand

b.best: Lower government spending and higher interest rates
